fields_add.community: Downstream of the Phase 1 dams, a separate compensation stream covered villages that lost river resources to the reduced flows. The World Bank's Phase 1B completion report says 54 communities in the river reaches nearest the dams received a first payment, with communities in reaches further down still being organised or to be assessed later through monitoring. One of the 54 is Bobete, in Thaba-Tseka district. It is represented by the U Khopo Maliba-Matšo Society, registered in 2003 and with over six hundred members, by the Court of Appeal's account. The losses the policy compensates, as the Society's founding affidavit lists them, are riverine resources, firewood and construction timber, fish resources, wild vegetables, medicinal plant resources and animal forage.
fields_add.outcome: The Bank's Phase 1B loan was IBRD-43390, US$45 million, approved 4 June 1998, effective 9 June 1999 and closed 31 December 2006, of which US$21.66 million was disbursed. During that project the scheme developed its Phase 1 In-Stream Flow Requirement policy: the Bank's completion report says the flow studies started in 1996 and were completed in 2001, and that the policy and its procedures were approved in June 2003. The policy paid out M27 million as a first ten-year payment to 54 downstream communities for predicted losses of natural resources, a payment the completion report says was made against presumed losses because the baseline data was too thin to predict ecosystem losses. The same report says compensation payments would continue, where still owed, for a further 40 years. Clause 7.7 of the policy, as quoted by the Court of Appeal, provides for two payments: the first for the period from the policy taking effect to 2013, and a second and final payment of the balance owing, calculated as a present value over 50 years and taking account of a ten-year review. The second payment did not come. The Lesotho Highlands Development Authority ran a monitoring programme from 2003 to 2013 and engaged consultants in 2013, whose report, dated 24 June 2014 in the Authority's answer and 4 June 2014 in its counsel's heads of argument, concluded there was no justification for a further payment; the Authority's panel of experts confirmed that, and the Authority decided not to pay. The Society sued in the High Court, where Makara J ordered the Authority to make the second and final payment. The Court of Appeal of Lesotho dismissed the Authority's appeal in C of A (CIV) 28/2025, heard 13 October 2025 and delivered 7 November 2025, before Mosito P, Sakoane CJ and Musonda AJA. The court held that the duty to compensate arises by operation of law, from section 17(1)(c) of the Constitution, Article 7(18) of the project Treaty and sections 44 to 46 of the Lesotho Highlands Development Authority Order 1986, and so cannot be negated or deferred by administrative policy. It held that the decision to discontinue compensation without meaningful consultation of the Bobete community was procedurally unfair and substantively unlawful. In his concurring judgment, at paragraph 49, Mosito P wrote: “Compensation delayed for over a decade is, in practical terms, compensation denied.” The judgment's flynote puts the same point as “compensation delayed for over a decade amounts to compensation denied”. The order confirmed the High Court's order and directed the Authority to commence payment within ninety days. The order does not state a sum; one of the questions the court set itself was whether an order to pay the “second and final tranche” is competent where no sum is quantified. GroundUp reported on 10 February 2026 that the ninety days expired on 7 February 2026 with no payment made, that the Society had received about M2.7 million for the first period and other associations between M500,000 and M3 million, and that the Authority's spokesperson Mpho Brown said the amount payable had not yet been finalised and remained subject to community engagement. GroundUp reported that on 20 October 2026 the High Court, before Acting Justice Tšebang Putsoane, made a settlement with the Authority an order of court: M89.9 million, payable within ninety days to 20 community associations, mostly in Thaba-Tseka, in individual amounts from M16.2 million down to M848,000, being the unpaid second tranche plus an 8 per cent increase since 2013.

extend.why: The Court of Appeal judgment of 7 November 2025 and the October 2026 M89.9 million settlement order concern the Phase 1 In-Stream Flow Requirement policy, which the World Bank's own Phase 1B completion report records as developed and first paid out during its IBRD-43390 loan, for flows taken by the Bank-financed Katse and Mohale dams.
